name: Niue

findings.local_actor: Telecom Niue Limited (state-owned enterprise), member of the Manatua Consortium
findings.financier: Government of Niue and New Zealand Aid Programme (Telecom Niue share)
findings.summary: The SubCom-built Manatua One Polynesia cable gave Niue its first submarine cable, replacing sole reliance on satellite; Telecom Niue holds Niue's share. The Niue government announced local ready-for-service in May 2021 after landing work at Makefu.

sources.publisher: Manatua Consortium press release (reposted by University of Hawaii PIREN)

findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: SubCom (US) supplied the cable, so pole us; consistent with COK-002. Dates conflict: the July 2020 consortium release lists Niue as live, while TV Niue reports the cable brought ashore at Makefu in December 2020 and government-declared ready for service on 13 May 2021; date set to the consortium RFS. TV Niue is a government-owned broadcaster, treated as S4, so single opened S1 carries medium. Values not stated.

findings.controller: Alepo (US; digital BSS and PCRF); Blue Arcus (California-based, role not specified)
findings.summary: Telecom Niue launched 4G in August 2018; vendor Alepo says it supplied the digital BSS with policy control (PCRF) in partnership with California-based Blue Arcus, and reported wide 4G uptake by mid-2019. Radio and core vendors are not named.
findings.analyst_inference: Only vendor marketing evidence. Alepo treated as US-controlled (corporate base assumed from general knowledge, not stated in the opened page) — reviewer should confirm. Covers billing/policy software only, not the RAN or packet core, so this says little about who can switch off the radio network.

findings.controller: Lenovo (ThinkAgile VX hardware, thin clients, laptops); VMware (vSAN/virtualisation software)
findings.local_actor: Government of Niue (all 22 departments, plus schools and the bank)
findings.summary: The Government of Niue consolidated its on-island IT onto a Lenovo ThinkAgile VX hyperconverged cluster running VMware vSAN, installed by NZ integrator Aiscorp, serving all 22 departments plus schools and the bank; older hardware became disaster recovery.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole left null: under the IT-equipment rule control is split between Lenovo hardware/firmware (PRC-headquartered) and VMware virtualisation software (US, Broadcom-owned); which dominates is a reviewer call. Coded as facilities because it is the government's primary compute platform, not a data-centre building. Intelligent CIO appears to relay the same case study, so not independent. Install date unknown; date is first report. A Lenovo-hosted case study surfaced in search but was not fetched (PRC vendor site).

findings.reversal_of: Unlicensed Starlink use in Niue via terminals bought in New Zealand
findings.summary: Niue's government declared Starlink use unauthorised under the Communications Act 1989, cited fines or jail for breaches, and in mid-May 2024 asked SpaceX to geo-block the service; Telecom Niue's CEO backed the restriction.
findings.analyst_inference: Reason coded regulatory (unlicensed operation under the 1989 Act); national security and protection of the local operator's investment were also cited, so a reviewer may prefer commercial or geopolitical. Tier 2 is a judgement: what was reversed was informal roaming use, not a contract. Superseded by the May 2026 temporary licence (NIU-005), hence still_current false.

findings.summary: Niue's government granted Starlink a temporary 12-month Spectrum and Internet Communications Licence as a trial, after regulatory and compliance checks, with monitoring of performance, national security and community impact; Telecom Niue continues separate fibre and site upgrades.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 because a licence was issued; it is temporary (trial to about May 2027), so in-force status at run date not separately confirmed. Single opened S1 carries medium. Reverses the 2024 restriction (NIU-004).

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase or deployment surfaced in other searches for a state of under 2,000 people

models.null_reason: one search found only a TV Niue report of an ICT policy consultation naming AI as an emerging technology; no provider partnership, government model adoption or sovereign model

applications.null_reason: two searches (China/Huawei/ZTE ICT assistance; police CCTV) returned nothing specific to Niue
